title: Schematicity of a relatively ample group quotient by a subtorus
statement: Let $S$ be a normal locally Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme] [pqf-def-locnoeth] [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Let $G\to S$ be a smooth separated commutative group scheme of finite presentation (here an $S$-group scheme is a group object in $S$-schemes, with multiplication, inverse and unit morphisms satisfying the group identities) [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] with connected geometric fibres [def-weil-connected-scheme]. Suppose $S$ has an affine open cover $\{W_i\}$ such that $G_{W_i}$ has an ample invertible module [def-sc-invertible-module] [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. Let $T\hookrightarrow G$ be a closed subgroup [def-weil-closed-immersion] which is a torus over $S$, meaning fppf locally isomorphic to $\mathbf G_m^r$ for finite locally constant $r\geq0$ [def-sc-gm-ga] [def-pc-fppf-site]. Suppose the fppf sheafification $F$ of $U\mapsto G(U)/T(U)$ on $S$-schemes is an algebraic space, and write $p:G\to F$ for the quotient map [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Then $F$ is represented by a smooth separated commutative $S$-group scheme of finite presentation, and $p$ is affine. The group law on $F$ is the one induced by multiplication of local lifts in $G$. Fibre products and restrictions use [def-pc-base-change] [def-pc-fibre-product]. No semiabelian-fibre hypothesis and no maximality or generic-fibre hypothesis on $T$ are imposed.

source.place: Chapter VI, §§1–2 (relatively quasi-projective homogeneous spaces), and Chapter IX, §2 (subtori). WANTED: original text and precise quotient representability statement; independently formulated supporting lemma.

proof.text: First work over one of the given affine opens $W\subseteq S$ with an ample module $L$ on $G_W$. An affine open of a locally Noetherian scheme is Noetherian. Apply [lem-sfb-normal-torus-finite-etale-splitting] to $T_W$: choose a finite étale surjection $u:W'\to W$ with $W'=\coprod_jW'_j$, a finite disjoint union of normal integral affine Noetherian schemes, on each of which $T$ splits. In particular $T_W$ is smooth, affine and finitely presented. All constructions of the quotient below are on the big fppf site: restricting to any base change gives the quotient of the pulled-back action, because quotient sections and equality of sections can both be checked after an fppf cover. We will construct a scheme representing $F_W$ and then glue these representations for the original opens $W$.

proof.text: Commutativity makes multiplication on cosets well defined: changing lifts $g_1,g_2$ to $g_1t_1,g_2t_2$ changes their product by $t_1t_2\in T$. Sheaf gluing therefore gives multiplication $F_W\times_WF_W\to F_W$, inverse and unit, with all group identities checked on local lifts; they are morphisms of algebraic spaces, which are natural transformations of their sheaves. Translation by $T_W$ on $G_W$ is free by cancellation. Apply [lem-sfb-free-flat-group-space-quotient] with $B=W$, $Z=G_W$, acting group $T_W$. Its hypotheses hold since $T_W$ is smooth and thus flat and locally finitely presented. It gives fppf local lifts and $T_W\times_WG_W\simeq G_W\times_{F_W}G_W$, $(t,g)\mapsto(tg,g)$. Consequently over every scheme test $V\to F_W$ an fppf cover trivializes $G_W\times_{F_W}V\to V$ as $T_W\times_WV\to V$: a chosen lift supplies the isomorphism by translation.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-space-four-property-fppf-descent] to the test morphisms in step 2: their trivializations are affine, being base changes of $T_W\to W$. Thus $p:G_W\to F_W$ is affine (each affine scheme test has affine scheme source). Apply [lem-sfb-space-smooth-surjective-fppf-locality] on the same scheme tests: their trivializations are smooth and surjective, so $p$ is smooth and universally surjective. Smoothness and affineness are preserved by base change; in particular these assertions hold for $p':G_{W'}\to F_{W'}$. An open $U\subseteq G_{W'}$ has open image in every scheme test of $F_{W'}$, by [lem-sfb-smooth-atlas-open-image] applied to this smooth surjective scheme atlas. Hence $p'(U)$ is an open subspace and $U\to p'(U)$ is a smooth surjection. Here algebraic spaces are viewed as discrete stacks: their sheaf axiom is precisely descent for objects and arrows in these discrete groupoids.

proof.text: Fix a component $W'_j$ and write $G'=G_{W'_j}$, $T'=T_{W'_j}$, $F'=F_{W'_j}$. The morphism $G'\to W'_j$ remains smooth and finitely presented; its geometric fibres remain connected, and it is nonempty because of the unit section. Thus [lem-sbc-smooth-connected-generic-geometry] shows that $G'$ is integral and normal. Since $W'_j\to W$ is finite, hence affine, $G'\to G_W$ is affine by base change. Pulling back $L$ along it gives an ample module on $G'$ by [lem-weil-pbc-pullback-ample-invertible]. Therefore [lem-sfb-relative-split-torus-invariant-affines] applies to the translation action of $T'\simeq\mathbf G_m^{r_j}$ and covers $G'$ by invariant affine opens $U_\alpha$. Their structure maps to $W'_j$ are of finite type: they are quasi-compact opens in the finite-type scheme $G'$ over a Noetherian base.

proof.text: For each $U_\alpha$ put $V_\alpha=p'(U_\alpha)$, an open subspace by step 3. It is saturated: a test point over $V_\alpha$ locally lifts to $U_\alpha$, and every other lift differs from it by a unique element of $T'$ by the torsor identity of step 2. Invariance of $U_\alpha$ implies that every such lift lies in $U_\alpha$; descent of membership in an open gives $p'^{-1}(V_\alpha)=U_\alpha$. The same identity and local lifts identify the sheaf $V_\alpha$ with the fppf quotient $U_\alpha/T'$. The action is still free on all tests. By [lem-sfb-affine-free-split-torus-invariants], this quotient is the affine scheme $\operatorname{Spec}(\Gamma(U_\alpha,\mathcal O)^{T'})$. These open affines cover $F'$. Their overlaps and identifications are already open subspaces of the same sheaf; gluing the affine schemes along those open subschemes yields a scheme $H'_j$. That $H'_j$ represents $F'$ is [lem-pc-schemes-criterion] applied to $F'$: it is an fppf, hence Zariski, sheaf; the $V_\alpha$ are representable subfunctors whose inclusions are representable by open immersions (step 3), and they cover $F'$ because the $U_\alpha$ cover $G'$ and $p'$ has fppf local lifts. This is exactly the local-scheme condition for the structure sheaf on an algebraic space, so the representing scheme has its original sheaf and quotient map.

proof.text: For later descent we check all hypotheses needed for ampleness of $H'_j$. The scheme map $p':G'\to H'_j$ is surjective, flat and locally finitely presented by step 2. Since $G'\to W'_j$ is smooth, [lem-sbc-smooth-flat-surjective-source-descent] makes $H'_j\to W'_j$ smooth. It has geometrically connected fibres, as each is the surjective continuous image of the connected geometric fibre of $G'$. To check separatedness, pull its diagonal back along $G'\times_{W'_j}G'\to H'_j\times_{W'_j}H'_j$. The result is $G'\times_{H'_j}G'\hookrightarrow G'\times_{W'_j}G'$, the inverse image of the closed subgroup $T'\hookrightarrow G'$ under $(g_1,g_2)\mapsto g_1g_2^{-1}$. It is closed by closed-immersion base change. The covering is a smooth surjection (products of $p'$), hence flat and locally finitely presented by smooth calculus and therefore fppf, hence fpqc, so [lem-pc-fpqc-descend-closed-immersion] makes the diagonal closed. Finally $G'$ is quasi-compact and surjects onto $H'_j$, so $H'_j$ is quasi-compact; its map to the affine base is quasi-compact. Separatedness implies quasi-separatedness. Smoothness implies local finite presentation, hence the structure map is finitely presented.

proof.text: The sheaf group law from step 2 is a group scheme law on $H'_j$, by representability. Step 6 verifies that this is a smooth separated group scheme of finite presentation with geometrically connected fibres over the normal integral affine Noetherian scheme $W'_j$. Apply [lem-sfb-affine-normal-connected-group-ample] to obtain an ample invertible module on all of $H'_j$. By [lem-sc-ample-finite-set-affine], every finite subset of $H'_j$ lies in an affine open. Put $H'=\coprod_jH'_j$, representing $F_{W'}$. A finite subset of $H'$ meets only finitely many components; choose such affine opens in those components and take their disjoint union, leaving the other components empty. A finite disjoint union of affine schemes is affine. Thus every finite subset of $H'$ lies in an affine open. This is a finite-subset statement on all of $H'$, not just fibrewise and not merely locally on its base.

proof.text: The identification $H'\simeq F_W\times_WW'$ supplies a canonical transport descent datum on $H'\to W'$ for the finite étale surjection $u:W'\to W$: both pullbacks to $W'\times_WW'$ identify with $F_W\times_W(W'\times_WW')$. The identity on this sheaf is an isomorphism of the two scheme pullbacks by Yoneda, and on triple products it satisfies the cocycle identity. Apply [lem-pd-invariant-affine-neighbourhoods], using the finite-subset property of step 7 and that $u$ is finite, flat, locally finitely presented and surjective. Every point of $H'$ then has a transport-invariant affine neighbourhood over an affine open of $W$. Apply [lem-pd-invariant-affine-descent-gluing] to this same datum: it is effective, giving a scheme $H_W\to W$ and an isomorphism $H_W\times_WW'\simeq H'$ compatible with the datum. No projectivity hypothesis or general claim that schematicity is étale-local on the base is used.

proof.text: The compatible identification after $W'\to W$ identifies the sheaf represented by $H_W$ with $F_W$. Explicitly, for every $W$-scheme $V$ use the finite étale, hence fppf and fpqc, cover $V\times_WW'\to V$. A section of either sheaf is exactly a section over this cover with equal pullbacks on its double overlap. On that equalizer the identification with $H'$ respects the same transport datum. The equalizers are therefore naturally bijective. The fppf sheaf property for $F_W$ is its hypothesis; the sheaf property for $h_{H_W}$ follows from [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent]. Hence $H_W$ represents $F_W$ and its quotient map is the original $p$.

proof.text: For each original affine $W$, repeat the scheme argument of step 6 with $G_W\to H_W$: the free-action quotient supplies a flat surjective locally finitely presented map, so smoothness of $G_W\to W$ descends by [lem-sbc-smooth-flat-surjective-source-descent]. The diagonal is closed by the difference-map test and fpqc closed-immersion descent, and quasi-compactness follows from the surjective image of the quasi-compact $G_W$. Thus $H_W\to W$ is smooth, separated and finitely presented. The local schemes $H_W$ agree on intersections since they represent restrictions of the same sheaf $F$; their unique representing isomorphisms satisfy the cocycle identity. Glue them to a scheme $H\to S$; it represents $F$ by [lem-pc-schemes-criterion], since $F$ is a Zariski sheaf and the open subfunctors $F_W\subseteq F$, representable by $H_W$ and with inclusions representable by open immersions (pullback of $W\subseteq S$), cover $F$. For smoothness use open-target restriction followed by smooth locality on the source. Local finite presentation is local by its definition; quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness can be tested over affine opens, each of which has a finite affine open refinement subordinate to the $W$. The closed-diagonal condition also restricts to this open cover. Thus $H\to S$ is smooth, separated and finitely presented. For global affineness of $p$, let $V\to F$ be an affine scheme test. The opens $V_W=V\times_SW$ form a Zariski, hence fppf, covering of $V$, and $G\times_FV_W\to V_W$ is the base change of the affine $p_W:G_W\to F_W$ of step 3, so affine; [lem-sfb-space-four-property-fppf-descent] (property affine) makes $G\times_FV\to V$ affine. Finally the multiplication, inverse and unit constructed from local lifts in step 2 are morphisms of this representing scheme and satisfy the commutative group identities. This is the required commutative $S$-group scheme, with exactly the specified quotient law.

lean.statement: theorem relatively_ample_subtorus_quotient_schematicity (S : Scheme.{u}) [IsLocallyNoetherian S] (hS : ∀ s : S, IsDomain (S.presheaf.stalk s) ∧ IsIntegrallyClosed (S.presheaf.stalk s)) (G : Over S) [CommGrpObj G] [Smooth G.hom] [IsSeparated G.hom] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation G.hom] [QuasiCompact G.hom] [GeometricallyConnected G.hom] (hample : ∃ (I : Type u) (W : I → S.Opens), (∀ s : S, ∃ i : I, s ∈ W i) ∧ ∀ i : I, IsAffineOpen (W i) ∧ ∃ (L : (G.hom ⁻¹ᵁ W i).toScheme.Modules) (hL : L.IsInvertible), @Scheme.Modules.IsAmple (G.hom ⁻¹ᵁ W i).toScheme L hL) (T : Over S) [GrpObj T] (i : T ⟶ G) [IsMonHom i] [IsClosedImmersion i.left] (hT : IsRelativeTorus T) (F : AlgebraicSpace S) (p : yoneda.obj G ⟶ F.obj.obj) (eta : coequalizer (yoneda.map (fst G T)) (yoneda.map (lift (fst G T) (snd G T ≫ i) ≫ μ[G])) ⟶ F.obj.obj) (hp : coequalizer.π _ _ ≫ eta = p) (hF : ∀ Z : Sheaf (Scheme.fppfTopology.over S) (Type u), Function.Bijective (fun f : F.obj.obj ⟶ Z.obj ↦ eta ≫ f)) : ∃ (H : Over S) (_ : CommGrpObj H) (q : G ⟶ H) (e : yoneda.obj H ≅ F.obj.obj), IsMonHom q ∧ yoneda.map q ≫ e.hom = p ∧ Smooth H.hom ∧ IsSeparated H.hom ∧ LocallyOfFinitePresentation H.hom ∧ QuasiCompact H.hom ∧ QuasiSeparated H.hom ∧ IsAffineHom q.left
